a transaction is a group of statements that succeed or fail together. atomicity means all or nothing, so a transfer can't debit one account without crediting the other. consistency means constraints still hold after it. isolation means two transactions running at once don't see each other's half-done work, so with the last ticket one buyer gets it and the other waits or fails. durability means once it's committed it survives a crash.
a transaction groups a few queries together so either all of them happen or none of them do.

relational databases have a fixed schema, joins and strong transactions, so they fit when the data is very connected and correctness matters, like payments or orders. document databases like mongo store flexible json documents, which fit when you read a whole object at once, the shape changes a lot, or you need to scale writes across machines, but you give up joins and often some consistency. I'd pick by how the data is related and queried.

you bundle a few changes so they either all land or none of them do, like moving money, you never take it out of one account without putting it in the other. while that bundle is running, somebody else's bundle can't see your half-finished state, so if two people grab the last seat at the same moment, one wins and the other is told no. and once the database says done, a power cut won't undo it.
